script.title: The 1833 Night Over 100,000 Meteors an Hour Fell
sentences: On the night of November 12, 1833, the sky started falling.
By one estimate, over 100,000 meteors an hour streaked across North America.
The Lakota reset their calendar around it, and the Cheyenne made a peace treaty.
Back then, scientists thought meteors formed inside the atmosphere itself.
Denison Olmsted gathered reports and saw every streak came from one point in Leo.
He guessed they came from a cloud of particles out in space.
By 1867, the source turned out to be dust from Comet Tempel-Tuttle.
That dust comes back every November, peaking around the 18th, so look up tonight.
script.description:
In 1833 the Leonids hit North America with over 100,000 meteors an hour by one estimate.
This week the same shower peaks again.
claims_en: The Leonid meteor storm happened on 12-13 November 1833
One estimate of the peak rate is over one hundred thousand meteors an hour
It was seen over North America
The Cheyenne established a peace treaty
Meteors had previously been thought to be atmospheric phenomena
Denison Olmsted collected reports and noted the meteors radiated from a point in the constellation of Leo
He speculated the meteors had originated from a cloud of particles in space
In 1866-67 information on Comet Tempel-Tuttle pointed to it as the source of the shower
The Leonids are an annual shower that tends to peak around 18 November
